complianceRule: Each feature is assessed at element, properties, relationships, and constraints levels. COMPLIANT is reserved for claims with passing automated semantic evidence at all applicable levels.
authorityNote: Cameo is an implementation benchmark only. No Cameo product behavior is asserted as an OMG SysML requirement in this evidence set.

evidence.feature: Requirement Diagram presentation of a Block, Requirement, and their Satisfy relationship

implementation.persistenceMapping: SysmlRepository.definitions, requirements, and relationships; diagramPresentations[diagramId].elementIds and presentations reference semantic IDs.

element.evidence: Automated tests create and present one Block and one Requirement.

properties.evidence: Block identity/name and Requirement requirementId/text are represented in the domain model and asserted by the semantic identity release gate.

relationships.evidence: Satisfy is stored with semantic sourceId/targetId endpoints and rendered when both endpoint presentations exist.

constraints.evidence: Endpoint and duplicate relationship admission are tested; this evidence does not cover the complete Requirement Diagram notation and constraint set in §16.3.1.1.

evidence.feature: One canonical semantic Block with independent diagram-scoped presentations, positions, and remove-from-diagram behavior

element.evidence: The release gate asserts one repository Block definition across Requirements and BDD.

properties.evidence: The release gate serializes/reloads different bounds for the same semantic ID on Requirements and BDD; the browser test verifies the positions remain independent after switching viewpoints.

relationships.evidence: Presentation records point to the same semantic ID; semantic identity and Satisfy endpoint preservation are independently tested by semanticIdentityReleaseGate.test.ts.

constraints.evidence: Canvas membership is scoped to its diagram; removeFromDiagram preserves the semantic definition and the other diagram presentation; duplicate membership is rejected by the gateway.

evidence.feature: Deleting a Block with an owned PartUsage (PartProperty representation), Satisfy relationship, and presentation requires impact confirmation and reports those impacts

implementation.validator: analyzeMutation computes descendants, removedRelationshipIds, and affected presentations; requiresDeletionConfirmation and executeSysmlCommand require a matching confirmedImpactHash before commit; validateSysmlRepository validates the resulting repository.
implementation.persistenceMapping: SysmlRepository.definitions, usages, relationships, and diagramPresentations; deletion removes owned semantic descendants, affected relationship IDs, and presentations in one gateway transaction.
implementation.projection: toExplorerImpact maps gateway impact into ExplorerImpact; MoveImpactDialog displays descendant, relationship, and presentation impacts before confirmation.

element.evidence: The browser test creates a Block, owned PartUsage (the V3 repository's PartProperty representation), Requirement, and Satisfy relationship; after confirmed deletion, the Block and owned PartUsage are absent while the Requirement remains.

properties.evidence: The PartUsage is created with the Block as owner and a valid Block type through the Model Explorer adapter; deletion impact reports it as a descendant.

relationships.evidence: The Satisfy relationship is displayed before deletion, included in Affected Relationships in the confirmation, and absent after confirmed deletion.

constraints.evidence: Unconfirmed material deletion is rejected with impact; the browser confirms using the returned impact hash, after which the single gateway transaction commits.

evidence.feature: A duplicate Satisfy relationship requested from a Model Explorer tree action is rejected without creating a duplicate and exposes its diagnostic

implementation.validator: validateCanonicalRelationshipCandidate returns DUPLICATE_RELATIONSHIP; executeSysmlCommand returns a non-committed diagnostic and preserves repository revision.
implementation.persistenceMapping: Accepted relationships are stored in SysmlRepository.relationships; the duplicate rejection commits no relationship and does not advance semantic revision.
implementation.projection: AppModelExplorer forwards ExplorerCommandResult through onCommandResult; App.tsx handleExplorerCommandResult routes error diagnostics to the visible error alert.

element.evidence: One valid Satisfy relationship remains after the duplicate request; the browser asserts exactly one relationship presentation.

properties.evidence: The original relationship retains its source, target, and kind; duplicate admission checks those identity-defining fields.

relationships.evidence: The rejected duplicate does not add a second relationship to the repository or diagram.

constraints.evidence: The gateway returns DUPLICATE_RELATIONSHIP and the browser verifies that code in a visible alertdialog.

evidence.feature: Motor semantic identity is preserved across BDD-A, BDD-B, Vehicle IBD, Requirement Diagram, Satisfy linkage, rename, and persistence round trip

element.evidence: The release gate asserts exactly one Motor Block, one leftMotor PartProperty, one REQ-001 Requirement, and one Satisfy relationship.

properties.evidence: Motor rename preserves its ID; leftMotor typeId remains Motor's ID; requirementId remains REQ-001 after round trip.

relationships.evidence: The Satisfy relationship retains its source and target IDs; BDD, IBD, and Requirement Diagram presentations reference the same semantic elements.

constraints.evidence: The release test verifies unique semantic counts, distinct diagram presentations, dynamic renamed-name resolution, and serialization/reload without duplication.
